metadata.description: Rules for distributing species coverage within vegetation strata based on ARI prominence codes

prominence_code_definitions.3.2: Highly likely or certain to have occurred; was prominent in some places (>5% cover)
prominence_code_definitions.3.1: Highly likely or certain to have occurred; at low cover
prominence_code_definitions.2.2: Quite likely occurred; if so, may have been prominent in some places (>5% cover)
prominence_code_definitions.2.1: Quite likely occurred; if so, at low cover

tree_canopy_layer.description: How to allocate tree canopy coverage among species

code_3.2.note: Prominent tree species dominate visual character and define the canopy

code_3.1.note: Present tree species scattered throughout, subdominant

shrub_layer.description: How to allocate shrub coverage among species

code_3.2.note: Fewer species dominate the shrub layer

code_3.1.note: More species diversity in understorey, but scattered

ground_layer.description: How to allocate groundcover among species

code_3.2.note: Dominant grasses like Themeda triandra can be near-monospecific

code_3.1.note: Many forbs and herbs contribute diversity

distribution_method.description: Step-by-step process for calculating species instances
steps: 1. Get total coverage for layer (e.g., tree_canopy_percent from vegetation_coverage_base.json)
2. Filter species by growth form (tree/shrub/ground) and prominence code (3.2/3.1)
3. Allocate coverage to 3.2 species first (60-80% of layer)
4. Allocate remaining coverage to 3.1 species (20-40% of layer)
5. Divide allocated coverage by typical crown size to get instance count
6. Round to nearest integer for practical rendering

example_calculation.vegetation_type: Grasslands and Woodlands on fertile plains

species_3.2.note: Large trees, so few instances needed
